_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Ch. 14 held at one clean, deliberate use (the tank water thick with bodies 'the way a jar goes thick with flies') — the draft reached for it twice more (Maria closing the register 'the way she'd close it over someone sleeping'; Edie's footsteps on the stair) and both were rewritten to 'like X' or cut, same discipline as ch. 12-13. Three chapters running at one or zero; the cap is holding.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Fifth chapter running at zero. The ch. 14 draft reached for it three times in the first pass (the nurse's tank, the extraction-theatre folder, the stud book) and every one was rewritten to name the actual object instead. Treat any return to this as a real lapse now.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: A ch. 14 draft pass reached for this once directly ('I have found, in every direction I've ever tested it, that knowing a thing happened costs almost exactly the same as watching it') and it was cut outright rather than banked — replaced with Edie simply carrying the stud book for both of them, no generalised rule stated. Stays on watch.

Ch. 14 landed at 22, same low-to-mid-20s band as ch. 7-13. Contrast rotated to a new pairing: Lloyd's spiralling, self-interrupting sentences against the flat closing lines of the extraction theatre's own case files ('result negative, subject retained') — institutional paperwork as the plain register, not another character's dialogue. Keep rotating the contrast partner rather than returning to the same one twice running.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: One clean, isolated use again (Lloyd's wrongness about Vantry's haze, 'same as most of what I'd decided about this city on no evidence at all'). Three of the last four chapters at exactly one use — occasional and controlled, not a default; no change in status.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Fourth chapter running clean of Lloyd narrating his own perception-management in filing language. Ch. 14 kept the filing/ledger register where it belongs — on the institution's own documents and on Edie's decision-making — and let Lloyd's self-management stay physical (keeping his face still, keeping the cold arm close to his side).

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Fourth chapter running without it. Not reached for in ch. 14 either; still safe to use if it arises naturally, not a default.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: Ch. 13 evolved away from this; ch. 14 confirms it — a draft pass produced three different trailing 'which was/is [judgment]' closes (the stolen moment on the stair, the specimen shelves, the final line) and all three were rewritten into separate declaratives or a plain 'like' comparison instead. Treat a return to the bare trailing-'which' shape as a real lapse, two chapters running now.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: Ch. 12 closed on Edie's cord going still; ch. 13 closed on Edie knotting off a thread and a one-word decision spoken aloud ('Thursday'); ch. 14 closed on Edie's line ('We're burning it') plus the concrete business of counting trips for the papers. Three chapters running on an object-plus-dialogue close instead — watch that this doesn't calcify into its own tic; the siege chapter (15) should probably end differently.

closers.pattern: chapter ends on an image of something indifferent or inanimate personified as 'patient', waiting out time without hurry
closers.example: the night came down slow over the burnt manse... patient, working at the dark the way it works at everything, given enough time and no one to tell it to stop
closers.note: Spent at ch. 08-09 review; stayed spent through ch. 13. Do not return to 'patient' as a chapter-ending word.
